sections.html:
Look for the Register of Deeds on the courthouse's main floor at 6 East Madison Avenue, Athens, TN 37303, or call (423) 745-1232. The counter serves the public from half past eight in the morning until four.

Staff record conveyances, deeds of trust, leases and similar instruments, and they certify copies of anything on file. Voters choose the register countywide every four years. Sellers rarely need to visit in person, since the closing agent normally sends in the deed that transfers your house. If you do go, bring the signed original and a way to pay the tax and recording charges.

The county's register page says the counter accepts debit and credit cards but not American Express. If your deed is long, ask the staff what the total will be.

With Athens as seat and largest city, McMinn County counted 57,404 residents in July 2025, up 7.8% from April 2020, with 24,424 housing units. Owner-occupants live in 75.8% of homes. A typical owner-occupied house is valued at $211,800, typical rent is $803, and the median household earns $61,470. There were 125 building permits in 2025.

Buyers ask about schools. McMinn County Schools runs both high schools, and Athens City Schools and the Etowah School District teach grades K through 8 within their own lines.

Recording brings two state taxes. Transfer tax is 37 cents per $100, figured on the higher of sale price or value. Mortgage tax is 11.5 cents per $100 borrowed, skipping the first $2,000 of debt. Both are collected at the counter, and the transfer tax falls on the grantee named in the deed.

What the McMinn County counter collects on state recording taxes
TaxRateWho pays by default
Transfer tax on real estate37 cents per $100 of price or valueGrantee (buyer)
Mortgage tax on borrowed money11.5 cents per $100, with the first $2,000 exemptBorrower
Receipt fee for the taxUp to $1 per receiptThe person filing

Contracts can move these costs onto the other side, so check yours before closing. Expect the closing agent to total both taxes and the recording charge for your deal.

sections.h2: What the register requires before recording
sections.html:
A posted checklist, Requirements to Record Documents, lists what the register looks for. Leave out an item and the deed may be rejected, so review it with the person preparing your closing papers.

  • Name and address of whoever prepared the deed, matching the return envelope if one is enclosed.
  • The buyer's address, plus the mailing address for future tax bills.
  • Map and parcel number, legal description, and last book and page of title.
  • Every signature notarized, with an acknowledgment that names the signers and bears the notary's seal and date.
  • A sworn oath of consideration giving the greater of the sale price or the property's value.
  • For any document tied to debt, the sentence "Maximum principal indebtedness for TN tax recording purposes is $___."

Corrections require new signatures and acknowledgments, or a scrivener's affidavit attached to the document. To get the original back, enclose a stamped, self-addressed return envelope; documents sent without one may be destroyed 90 days after recording. Also check the spelling of every name against the prior deed, since a mismatch can slow indexing.

sections.h2: Transfers with no realty transfer tax
sections.html:
Tennessee's recordation manual carves out some transfers from the $0.37 tax. A few of them show up in family and estate sales, and an exempt transfer does not need the sworn oath.

  • Conveying a leasehold estate.
  • Deeds between spouses at the start or end of a tenancy by the entirety.
  • A deed by an executor fulfilling a gift left in a will.
  • Divorce decrees, and deeds that settle property rights between spouses.
  • Putting a house into, or taking it out of, a revocable living trust the owner or spouse made.
  • Conveyances involving a government body.

A quitclaim deed is taxed on whatever consideration was given, but the state taxes fair market value if the wording shows an intent to convey the property itself, such as "in fee simple." State revenue staff occasionally sample deeds from a random county and date range, compare the sworn value with the assessor's figure, and send an inquiry letter when they differ widely. A McMinn County deed showing an unusually low price can draw one.

You will probably never log in to these systems yourself. A title company or attorney uploads the signed deed, and the register's staff record it and send it back.

E-recording comes in through Simplifile, Corporation Service Company (CSC) or eRecording Partners Network (EPN), and your title company will choose among them at closing.

For searching, the county points researchers to US Title Search Network, which charges per search or a monthly fee. If that service gives you trouble, the register's page lists Progress Inc. at 1 (800) 394-7477. Assessor data is separate: the Assessor of Property, at (423) 745-2743, keeps parcel maps and property cards, and the state's assessment website lets you look up the map and parcel numbers that every conveyance needs.

If you inherited a McMinn County house and need to sell, ask the register how the executor's deed should be worded, and ask the probate clerk for proof of authority.

sections.h2: Property tax when a McMinn County house sells
sections.html:
Pay county property tax to the McMinn County Trustee at the courthouse, 6 East Madison Avenue, (423) 745-1291. Payment of the current bill runs from October 1 through the end of February, on weekdays from 8 to 4, with Saturday mornings added in February.

The Trustee also handles applications for the state's Tax Relief Program, which helps elderly and disabled homeowners and disabled-veteran owners. Applications close 35 days after the February 28 payment deadline. Relief repays part of a bill you have paid, so the bill still arrives.

How the current year's tax is split gets decided at closing, so bring it up with the closing agent early and get a payoff from the Trustee first. A wrong owner name or mailing address on the roll is the assessor's to fix. After the deed is recorded here, the sale is public record, and the title company can confirm that no earlier lien remains open. If you are selling an inherited house or one with back taxes, ask for the payoff in writing so the figure on the settlement statement matches it. Keep in the file the Trustee's receipt, the recorded deed and the closing statement, since together they show who paid what and when.

faqs.q: Where is a McMinn County deed recorded?
faqs.a: The McMinn County Register of Deeds, located in the Athens courthouse at 6 East Madison Avenue, takes it. Questions go to (423) 745-1232. Title companies usually submit deeds electronically.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax applies when a McMinn County house sells?
faqs.a: The rate is 37 cents on every $100 of price or value, whichever is larger. The buyer owes it unless the contract says otherwise.

faqs.q: Can a deed be e-recorded in McMinn County?
faqs.a: Yes, through Simplifile, CSC or eRecording Partners Network. Individuals without an account normally go through a title company or attorney.

faqs.q: Is transfer tax owed on a sale of an inherited McMinn County house?
faqs.a: An executor's deed carrying out a gift in a will is exempt, but the later sale to a buyer is taxed normally. Ask the register how each deed in the chain is treated.

faqs.q: Where is McMinn County property tax paid ahead of a closing?
faqs.a: Call the McMinn County Trustee at (423) 745-1291 for a payoff and pay at the Athens courthouse. Current-year bills can be paid from October 1 through the end of February.
